claim: IEEE 1588/PTP support in GigE Vision is a GEV 2.0 feature (capability bit 0x00080000 in 0x0934, enable bit 0x00080000 in GVCP Configuration 0x0954, clock status in 0x096C low 4 bits); GEV 2.1 added profile registers 0x0974-0x097C. So single-cable PTP sync does not require GigE Vision 3.0.
how_verified: read-code (Wireshark GVCP dissector field names/masks tagged _v2_0/_v2_1)

claim: GVCP command codes: DISCOVERY 0x0002/3, FORCEIP 0x0004/5, PACKETRESEND 0x0040, READREG 0x0080/1, WRITEREG 0x0082/3, READMEM 0x0084/5, WRITEMEM 0x0086/7, PENDING_ACK 0x0089, EVENT 0x00C0, ACTION 0x0100/1; Aravis' enum lacks FORCEIP and ACTION and labels 0x0004 as BYE_CMD.

claim: PACKETRESEND payload: standard IDs {u16 channel, u16 block_id, u32 first(24b), u32 last(24b)}; extended IDs {u32 0, u32 first, u32 last, u64 block_id} with header flag 0x10. GVSP extended-ID header is status u16, flags u16, infos u32 (bit31 EI), block_id u64, packet_id u32.

claim: ACTION_CMD payload is device_key, group_key, group_mask plus an optional 64-bit action time when GVCP header flag 0x80 (scheduled) is set; capability bits: action 0x40, scheduled action 0x00020000. Of the open-source clients examined, only viva-genicam implements action commands (telegenic stops at EVENTDATA; pyGigEVision has none).
how_verified: read-code (grep of pyGigEVision for ACTION/0x0100 returned nothing)

claim: GVSP frames are uncompressed by default (payload type 1 = image in a PFNC pixel format); GEV 2.0 also defines JPEG (6), JPEG2000 (7), H.264 (8); each image leader carries a 64-bit device timestamp, pixel format, width and height.
how_verified: read-code + ran-test (probe decoded payload_type=1, pixel_format 0x1080001 Mono8 and leader timestamps from fake camera)

claim: In a real camera XML (Hikrobot, vendored in telegenic tests), SFNC GevIEEE1588 maps to Bit 12 of StructReg at 0x0954 (= mask 0x00080000 under GenApi BigEndian bit numbering) and GevIEEE1588Status maps to MaskedIntReg 0x096C LSB31/MSB28 (= mask 0xF), i.e. PTP features are thin GenApi wrappers over bootstrap registers.
how_verified: read-code (parsed XML with ElementTree and cross-checked masks against Wireshark)

claim: Socket buffer limits cause loss: Linux SO_RCVBUF is capped by net.core.rmem_max (16 MiB request -> 425,984 B) and SO_RCVBUFFORCE (CAP_NET_ADMIN) bypasses it; with the cap, MTU9000 at 1 Gbit/s dropped 7.2% (default buffer) and against the fake camera 641 kernel RcvbufErrors / 3-of-53 complete frames at only 50 Mbit/s, vs 0 errors / 75-of-75 with a forced 32 MiB buffer. macOS caps at kern.ipc.maxsockbuf (SB_MAX 8 MiB default); Windows default measured 64 KiB.
how_verified: ran-test (bench_linux_docker_*.txt, results/fake_probe_default_rcvbuf.txt vs forced) + read-spec/doc
